title: Run @PostConstruct and @PreDestroy callbacks in order

blocks.text: Spring's step 6 (Q1) calls `@PostConstruct` methods after creating a bean and `@PreDestroy` methods before discarding it. The page's version reads both annotations through reflection and runs the methods sorted by their `order()`.

items: `initialize(Object target)`: call every no-argument method `target`'s class declares with `@PostConstruct`, lowest `order` first.

blocks.text: Callbacks may be `private`, and **private callbacks run too**. When a callback throws, `Method.invoke` wraps the exception in `InvocationTargetException`; **rethrow the callback's own exception** instead.

rows: seven callbacks with orders 0 to 6, declared in another order

cases.says: initialize() runs seven @PostConstruct methods lowest order first, and the same seven names with reversed orders run in reverse, whatever order reflection lists them in; destroy() runs flushBuffers (1) then closeConnections (2).
A private @PostConstruct method is run as well.
A @PostConstruct method that throws IllegalStateException("no config") makes initialize() throw that same exception, not a wrapper.

concepts: A container calls @PostConstruct methods after creating a bean and @PreDestroy methods before discarding it.
Method.invoke wraps the target's exception in InvocationTargetException; the handler rethrows its cause, or a proxy's caller gets UndeclaredThrowableException.
